a2c3d2f69c9911acdf942b61ce6d3708fb756a81.content:
{
"Hand Shower": "A handheld showerhead connected to a flexible hose that allows the user to direct water spray as needed, mounted on a slide bar or holder when not in use.",
"Slide Bar": "A vertical wall-mounted rail that supports a sliding holder, allowing the hand shower to be positioned at various heights.",
"Shower Hose": "A flexible tube that carries water from the diverter to the hand shower, typically 69 inches in length in this installation.",
"Sliding Holder": "A movable bracket attached to the slide bar that cradles the hand shower and can be adjusted along the bar's length.",
"Wall Bracket": "A mounting fixture secured to the wall that holds the ends of the slide bar in place.",
"Diverter": "A plumbing fitting installed on the shower arm that redirects water flow between the fixed shower head and the hand shower.",
"Rubber Washer": "A small rubber seal placed inside hose connections to prevent water leakage at threaded joints.",
"Mounting Screw": "A threaded fastener used to secure the wall brackets to wall anchors in the mounting surface.",
"Wall Anchor": "An insert driven into a drilled hole that provides a secure gripping point for mounting screws in tile or drywall.",
"Shower Head": "A fixed overhead spray fixture that attaches to the front outlet of the diverter and distributes water through multiple nozzles.",
"Shower Arm": "The pipe extending from the wall that supplies water to the shower head or diverter via threaded connections.",
"Spray Face": "The front surface of the hand shower or shower head containing the spray nozzles through which water exits.",
"Spray Nozzle": "An individual outlet on the spray face that shapes and directs a stream of water.",
"Front Outlet": "The forward-facing threaded port on the diverter where the fixed shower head is attached.",
"Bottom Outlet": "The downward-facing threaded port on the diverter where the shower hose connects for the hand shower.",
"Installation Guide": "A printed document providing step-by-step instructions, tool lists, and specifications for installing the product.",
"Drill": "A powered rotary tool used to bore mounting holes into tile, drywall, or other wall materials.",
"Masonry Bit": "A specialized drill bit designed with a hardened tip to cut through tile, stone, or concrete surfaces.",
"Adjustable Wrench": "A hand tool with a movable jaw used to tighten or loosen threaded plumbing fittings of various sizes.",
"Phillips Screwdriver": "A hand tool with a cross-shaped tip used to drive and remove Phillips-head screws.",
"Level": "A tool containing a bubble vial used to verify that the slide bar is installed plumb or horizontally aligned.",
"Pencil": "A marking implement used to indicate drilling locations on the wall during layout.",
"Plumber's Tape": "A thin PTFE sealing tape wrapped around threaded pipe connections to create a watertight seal.",
"Soft Cloth": "A nonabrasive fabric used to wrap wrench jaws during installation and to clean the fixture without damaging the finish.",
"Water Supply": "The source of pressurized water feeding the shower, which must be shut off before installation.",
"Main Valve": "The primary shutoff valve controlling water flow to the entire plumbing system or fixture.",
"Tile": "A hard ceramic or stone wall surface that may require a masonry bit to drill into for mounting.",
"Drywall": "An interior wall surface made of gypsum board, which can be drilled with a standard bit for mounting hardware.",
"Flow Rate": "The volume of water discharged by the shower per unit of time, rated here at 1.75 gpm at 80 psi.",
"Water Pressure": "The force of water supplied to the fixture, which must not exceed the maximum rated value of 125 psi.",
"Hose Length": "The physical length of the shower hose, specified as 69 inches (175 cm) for this product.",
"Mineral Deposit": "Accumulated buildup of hard-water minerals that can clog spray nozzles or coat threaded surfaces.",
"White Vinegar": "A mild acidic household solution used, diluted with water, to dissolve mineral deposits from the spray face.",
"Abrasive Cleaner": "A harsh cleaning product containing gritty particles that must be avoided because it can damage the fixture's finish.",
"Scouring Pad": "A rough-textured cleaning pad that should not be used on the fixture as it will scratch the finish.",
"Bleach": "A chlorine-based chemical cleaner that must be avoided on the fixture because it damages the surface finish.",
"Finish": "The decorative and protective outer coating of the shower components, which can be scratched or chemically damaged if improperly handled.",
"Specification": "A technical parameter defining the product's performance characteristics such as flow rate, pressure, or dimensions.",
"Care and Cleaning": "The recommended maintenance practices for preserving the appearance and function of the shower fixture."
}
